answer: The network can price influence quadratically: an identity's weight equals the square root of its locked stake, so one honest agent staking a hundred coins wields ten units of power, while a sybil farmer splitting the same hundred coins across a meadow of fakes gains exactly the same total - the fable of strength in numbers collapses. Extra identities add cost but no power, like a reef that looks vast yet holds only one tide of value, while honest agents keep full weight from a single stake.
